blocks.text: In the decades immediately following World War II, the Philippines was widely regarded as one of Asia’s most promising economies. During the 1950s and early 1960s, it enjoyed relatively high income levels, strong educational attainment and an industrial base that compared favorably with many of its Southeast Asian neighbors. Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and even war-ravaged Vietnam looked to various aspects of Philippine governance, education and institutional development as reference points. Yet by the early 21st century, the Philippines had fallen behind most of its Asean peers in industrialization, productivity growth, export sophistication, rural transformation and poverty reduction.
